A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adam loss-spike mechanism and retain identifiable equations, experiments, and figures. Their text, mathematical content, figures, and appendices are readable, allowing additions to be distinguished from relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original quadratic-optimization experiments and neural-network training results for function approximation, CIFAR-10, and synthetic sequence tasks, including supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds results for MNIST, SlimPajama language modeling, additional architectures and optimizers, and controlled sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: Adam's update, the preconditioned Hessian in Eq. (7), the gradient-directional predictor, and its sustained version remain unchanged. However, v2 adds an Adafactor-specific preconditioned-curvature construction incorporating its scaling and clipping factors (Fig. D17), a limited adaptation of the diagnostic.

E1.justification: v2 adds MNIST image classification (Fig. D7) and natural-language next-token training on a 100B-token SlimPajama split (Sec. 6.2). This substantially extends coverage beyond v1's function approximation, CIFAR-10, and synthetic sequence tasks. The earlier CIFAR-10 and anchor-task experiments remain in the appendices.

E2.justification: v2 extends the controlled quadratic-optimization comparisons with evaluated AdaGrad, RMSProp, and Adafactor experiments (Figs. D15–D17). These additions are confined to supplementary quadratic tests; GD and the existing maximum-eigenvalue and update-directional-curvature comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include a 187M-parameter Transformer with batch size 512 and gradient clipping, ViT/ResNet18 evaluations, and momentum-free beta2 sweeps. Fig. 3 adds a coupled case with beta1=0.6 and beta2=0.5; the earlier case survives in Fig. D21. Fig. 4's reported width changes from 1,000 to 20, but inconsistent v1 descriptions and retained curves do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial mechanism checks: beta2 mitigation experiments in Transformers, a beta1=0 sweep isolating adaptive dynamics (Fig. D22), multiple unstable eigendirections (Fig. D18), a test of the rounding-error explanation (Fig. D20), and larger-learning-rate sensitivity (Fig. D21). Earlier epsilon/clipping interventions and spike-type case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional trajectories and decay fits in v2 do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including MNIST spike trajectories, reduced spike frequency at lower beta2 in the 187M Transformer, and contrasting AdaGrad/RMSProp/Adafactor dynamics. These are newly reported experiments, not improvements over matched v1 runs. Retained findings, such as FNN threshold crossing at epoch 179, spike onset at 184, and recovery at 206, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds a local GD descent proposition, an exact loss-increase criterion using a path-averaged Hessian (Theorem D.1), and a decaying-learning-rate instability theorem. It also revises the momentum stability statement to require positive directional curvature and substantially reworks the existing five-stage theorem with additional assumptions, transition definitions, and finiteness arguments.

C1.justification: The central scientific claims remain: adaptive preconditioner dynamics can independently trigger spikes, persistent second-moment decay sustains instability, and gradient-directional curvature predicts spikes better than maximum curvature alone. The five-stage mechanism and lower-beta2 mitigation idea already appear in v1; v2 emphasizes them and supplies broader supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly introduces the frozen-time approximation and timescale-separation justification, distinguishes positive-curvature overshooting from saddle escape, and explains why increasing beta1 offers limited protection. It also adds substantive qualifications about one-dimensional theoretical guarantees, stochastic minibatch prediction noise, and computational limits beyond roughly 200M parameters.

D1.justification: v2 adds the large-Transformer hyperparameter table, ViT/ResNet and Adafactor settings, and details about power-iteration counts and Hessian-vector-product costs. It newly states that code accompanies supplementary materials, without verifiable access in these PDFs. Conversely, v1's dedicated Fig. 4 setup, including initialization distributions and separate network widths, is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds central-flow research, recent Adam convergence/ODE studies, and language-model and reasoning-task references, while clarifying its relationship to adaptive Edge of Stability. It removes Cattaneo and Shigida's lower-beta2 citation. These update the positioning without replacing the existing related-work framework.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, stability explanation, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around decoupling and explicit qualifications. The former five-phase subsection becomes a standalone section, CNN discussion moves into the appendix, and the appendices are reorganized with new disclosure sections. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, redraws Fig. 3 to display moment–gradient coupling, adds an overshooting illustration and five-stage diagrams, and reorganizes Fig. 7. Numerous new experimental figures and a hyperparameter table accompany these changes. Earlier CNN plots are relocated rather than removed.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is stronger testing of the mechanism beyond v1's predominantly toy, synthetic, and small-image-subset experiments. Natural-language training, additional architectures, and controls for momentum and alternative explanations materially strengthen empirical support. Explicit approximation and applicability limits also improve interpretation. The removed Fig. 4 setup and remaining theoretical inconsistencies, including Theorem 5.1 omitting an assumption required by Appendix D.2, temper but do not outweigh these substantial gains.
